summary.headline: Foods & Inns posted a forex loss of INR106 million in Q2 FY27 from forward contracts, with ~3,300 MT unshipped orders expected to clear in Q3.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by a notional forex loss of INR106 million (about INR10 crores), booked in other expenses, from forward cover on export sales as the rupee depreciated and shipments slipped. Dispatches were delayed by container unavailability and high freight rates, but October saw a substantial pickup, with about 60% of the ~3,300 MT unshipped orders shipped that month. Management said there are no cancellations, only deferrals, and expects all carry-over execution in Q3. The company has stopped booking new forward covers since April and is discussing possible bank penalties.

financial_highlights.change: First quarterly loss from forex in many years; booked in other expenses

financial_highlights.metric: Mark-to-market loss in consolidated cash flow
financial_highlights.change: Balance of forex loss attributed to sales vs realisation difference
Up from INR53 crores at March; new central bank long-term facility repayable over 4 years
Last year ~INR28-30 crores; FY27 application filed, timing uncertain

financial_highlights.metric: Green Top brand monthly sales (North India)

segments.name: Pulping (Mango, Guava, Papaya, Tomato)
segments.commentary: Pulping contributes 80%+ of revenue. Company claims No. 1 position in mango pulp; Alphonso premium exports to Japan and France, while Totapuri earns better margins domestically. Pricing power limited by long rupee hedges.

segments.name: Frozen foods
segments.commentary: Export margins are better than domestic. Management expects 25-30% average growth over the next 3 years, with GCC demand rising and a Saudi customer tie-up for frozen mango pulp and vegetables. Capacity is fully utilised; a 3x expansion target is set over 3 years with a 35-38% government capital subsidy.

segments.name: Spray Drying
segments.commentary: October 2026 was the record month, with ~100 MT sold. H2 volume is guided above 550 MT (18-19% annualised volume growth), value growth just under 10%, and EBITDA margin about 18%. Capacity addition of ~120 MT per annum is due for commercial production by end-January 2027.

segments.name: Frozen and other segments (combined)
segments.commentary: Management said frozen, spray drying and other segments together are growing around 20% of revenue. Kusum spices is a separate company and is excluded from the standalone numbers.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 overall volume growth expected at 17-18% YoY; 18-19% volume growth in Spray Drying. No revenue guidance, as the company works on cost-plus pricing and raw-material prices are volatile.
Unshipped orders (~3,300 MT) expected to be fully shipped in Q3 FY27; freight rates and vessel availability are softening.
Forex: company has stopped forward cover since April 2026 and will meet banks after Diwali on any penal interest; quantum not yet known.
Subsidy: DGFT extended timelines by 45 days; FY27 application under ministry consideration, with an update expected next quarter.
Management said the worst is over and the stock is at the bottom, but gave no guarantees.
capex_capacity: Spray Drying capacity addition of ~120 MT per annum; commercial production targeted for mid to end-January 2027.
Gujarat warehousing expansion due for completion by mid-December 2026.
Capital WIP closing balance about INR25 crores; management said there is no other capex planned at this stage.
Frozen segment capacity fully utilised; plan to reach 3x frozen capacity within 3 years, with a 35-38% government capital subsidy approved in principle.
Cash flow shows INR41 crores of acquisition of tangible and intangible assets; management could not explain it on the call and promised a follow-up.
demand_pricing: Export demand intact with no cancellations; deferrals only. European cold-storage losses may create urgent supply demand later.
Pricing is cost-plus. Spray Drying and frozen have passed through inflation; pulping has not fully, because of long-held rupee hedges, and talks with brands are ongoing.
Spray Drying realisations expected to fall as vegetable and fruit raw-material costs eased over two years.

Cluster development scheme under the National Horticulture Board (one of 12 companies selected, inaugurated 30 October) will onboard ~15,000 farmers in Nashik for raw-material security and pesticide control.
Government spice ban on loose spices expected to help branded packaged players; company is pursuing a hybrid white-label and private-label model.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~3,300 MT unshipped orders has shipped, and will it all be recognised in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% shipped in October; all carry-over expected to complete in Q3. No penalty clauses as contracts are FOB; one freak shipping surcharge was settled by the customer.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the forex loss and will hedging policy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss arose from forward contracts used for RBI-mandated export hedging, plus delayed shipments that missed maturity dates. Since April 2026 no new forwards are booked, and the Board has advised against them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 plan for Spray Drying and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 Spray Drying volume is guided above 550 MT, with ~120 MT capacity coming online by end-January 2027, a Gujarat warehouse by mid-December, and EBITDA around 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-current borrowings rise, and is more borrowing needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rise to INR91 crores reflects a central bank long-term facility availed during shipment delays, repayable over 4 years. Management said no further borrowing is needed and short-term borrowing should fall by March.

qa_highlights.question: What subsidy income should be expected this year?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR84 crores received over the last 4 years; last year's receipt was INR28-30 crores; this year's application is in a similar range but timing is uncertain and recognised on cash basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company rethinking pricing and margins given rising overheads?
qa_highlights.answer: Frozen and Spray Drying have captured inflation; pulping has not, and brand discussions are ongoing. Export frozen margins are better than domestic, while Totapuri domestic margins beat export.

risks_watch: Forex exposure: no hedging going forward, so rupee moves hit realisation; possible penal interest from banks is unquantified.
Pulping pricing: inability to pass through inflation on pulp, with overheads rising fast, could compress EBITDA per tonne.
Subsidy: ~INR28-30 crore annual subsidy depends on ministry approval, which is still pending.
Freight and container availability: recovery is expected but not assured; Q3 and Q4 carry-over and domestic Q4 dispatch depend on it.
Unexplained INR41 crore investing outflow for tangible and intangible assets; follow-up pending.
Minority concern: stock at historical lows; promoter stated intent to consolidate but gave no timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and Q3 recovery, with explicit tone of course correction on forex; defensive and evasive on specifics, declining revenue guidance, not disclosing the forex penalty quantum, and deferring the INR41 crore cash flow query and subsidy timing.
key_quotes: So as a company, we have now decided not to do any forward cover, keep it open.
In a single month, we are able to sell 100 metric tons, which is a phenomenal.

adds.what: Spray Drying capacity addition of ~120 MT per annum
Frozen segment capacity to 3x over 3 years (35-38% govt capital subsidy approved in principle)
Gujarat warehousing expansion (storage, not productive capacity)

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 overall volume growth of 17-18% and Spray Drying volume above 550 MT (18-19%), with no revenue guidance; backing is partial, citing ~120 MT/yr Spray Drying capacity due by end-January 2027, ~3,300 MT unshipped orders (about 60% shipped in October) to clear in Q3, and a 3x frozen target over 3 years that is not yet specific.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spray Drying EBITDA guided at about 18% and frozen/Spray Drying have passed through inflation, but pulping has not (long rupee hedges), and the INR10 crore forex loss and no further hedging add risk to margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spray Drying capacity addition of ~120 MT per annum is under construction with commercial production targeted for mid to end-January 2027, and the Gujarat warehouse is due by mid-December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 overall volume growth of 17-18% and Spray Drying above 550 MT (18-19%), with ~3,300 MT unshipped orders (about 60% shipped in October) expected to clear in Q3.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Frozen capacity is fully utilised and management targets 3x frozen capacity over 3 years with a 35-38% government subsidy approved in principle, but management said no other capex is planned at this stage and the INR41 crore cash outflow is unexplained.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue guidance is given, and management declined to commit beyond volume growth, saying raw-material prices are volatile and the worst is over without guarantees.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Carry-over shipments depend on freight and container availability, possible penal interest from banks is unquantified, and the subsidy (~INR28-30 crore last year) is pending ministry approval.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Green Top brand is at an early stage at ~INR60-70 lakhs monthly sales in North India and a Saudi frozen mango pulp and vegetables tie-up is mentioned, but no dated product launch was guided.

rows.label: Unshipped orders clear in Q3 FY27
rows.why: About 3,300 MT of unshipped orders with about 60% shipped in October, and management expects full carry-over completion in Q3 with no cancellations, only deferrals.

rows.label: Govt subsidy application (FY27)
rows.why: Last year's subsidy was INR28-30 crore and the FY27 application is under ministry consideration with an update expected next quarter, but timing is uncertain and it is recognised on a cash basis.

rows.label: Short-term borrowing to fall by March
rows.why: Management said no further borrowing is needed and short-term borrowing should fall by March, after non-current borrowings rose to INR91 crore from INR53 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q3 catch-up, Spray Drying volumes and the January capacity addition, but cautious and evasive on revenue guidance, the forex penalty quantum, the INR41 crore investing outflow and subsidy timing; analysts pressed on forex hedging, pulping pricing and cash flow.
